Year three (20 BBY–19 BBY)

The apprentices of Count Dooku

"You have failed me for the last time. You are no longer my apprentice. And now, you shall die."
―Dooku betrays Asajj Ventress, sparking a chain of events leading to the ascension of Savage Opress[31]

As the war's second year progressed, a cycle of betrayals and vengeance consumed the Sith hierarchy, which in turn affected a number of campaigns between the Confederacy and the Republic.[31] At the Battle of Sullust,[204] Asajj Ventress spearheaded the Separatist navy's strike on a Republic fleet. Flying her personal Ginivex-class fanblade starfighter, Ventress led the droid tri-fighters of Trident groups one and two in overwhelming the Resolute.[31] Wullf Yularen narrowly escaped from his flagship before it went down.[205] Building on her success, Ventress gave chase to Obi-Wan Kenobi and Anakin Skywalker in their Delta-7B interceptors. However, both Kenobi and Ventress crashed in the hangar of the Separatist command ship, with Skywalker following them there.[31]

From afar, Darth Sidious sensed Ventress's growing power in the Force, and he recognized her as a threat. Suspecting that Dooku was training Ventress as a means of supplanting him, Sidious demanded that Dooku prove his allegiance to him by eliminating Ventress. Though reluctant to do so, Dooku obeyed his Master's wishes. Dooku recalled Confederate reinforcements that were inbound to the Sullust system, then betrayed Ventress by informing her that she was no longer his apprentice—and that she would die. Shell-shocked from Dooku's betrayal, Ventress dueled Kenobi and Skywalker until Dooku ordered TJ-912, the tactical droid in charge of the Separatist armada over Sullust, to sacrifice their flagship and obliterate it.[31]

Kenobi and Skywalker made it off the enemy command ship,[31] but both they[204] and Dooku presumed that Ventress died when the Providence-class Dreadnought was destroyed from friendly fire. Afterward, Dooku had TJ-912 withdraw their fleet from the Sullust system, conceding victory to the Republic. In actuality, Ventress had survived, albeit barely. Captain Ratch and his band of scavengers found her in the wreckage of her starfighter and brought her aboard their freighter,[31] the Raider.[205] Ventress slew Ratch and his crew and returned home to Dathomir, where her people, the Nightsisters, nursed her back to health. When Ventress and her fellow Nightsisters Naa'leth and Karis failed to assassinate Dooku at his palace on Serenno, Ventress conspired with Mother Talzin, the leader of her Nightsister clan, to exact her revenge on Dooku by different means.[31]

From Dathomir's village of subservient Nightbrothers, Ventress procured a formidable warrior who would replace her as Dooku's next apprentice: Savage Opress. Before gifting Opress to Dooku, Talzin and her Nightsister witches imbued Opress with their magicks, bringing him under their control. Officially, Talzin declined Dooku's proposal for an alliance between the Nightsisters and the Confederacy, as her clan had no interest in becoming involved in the Clone Wars;[206] although some Nightsisters were seen fighting for the Separatist cause during the war,[207] a formal alliance never emerged.[208] In any case, Dooku opted to assess Opress's abilities by sending him to an active battlefront on Devaron. There, the Separatist Droid Army was laying siege to the Temple of Eedit, a Jedi temple that doubled as an outpost for the Grand Army. Opress was the sole survivor of the battle, as he butchered[206] Clone Commander Trauma[209] and his clone soldiers, as well as Jedi Master Halsey and his Padawan, Knox.[206]

Impressed by Opress's performance,[206] Dooku trained his new apprentice in the ways of the Sith,[204] hoping to depose Sidious in accordance with the Rule of Two.[206] Opress's next task was to abduct King Katuunko of Toydaria, for Dooku still harbored a grudge against Katuunko[204] due to the latter's refusal to ally Toydaria with the Confederacy.[91] However, Opress's massacre on Devaron had caught the attention of the Jedi High Council.[204] After Delta Squad, a clone commando unit composed of Sergeant Boss, Fixer, Sev, and Scorch,[210] recovered Halsey's and Knox's bodies from the Temple of Eedit, Kenobi and Skywalker went to investigate Opress's connection to Dathomir. The two Jedi headed to Toydaria after learning from Talzin that Opress was currently there.[204]

Everything came to a head at Toydaria. Opress cut through the Toydarian Royal Palace's royal guards, but when Kenobi and Skywalker interfered, Opress Force-choked Katuunko to death. When Opress brought Katuunko's corpse aboard Dooku's Providence-class Dreadnought in orbit of Toydaria, Dooku was furious that Opress had disobeyed his orders to keep Katuunko alive. At that moment, Ventress entered Dooku's chambers and activated the spell that ensured Opress's loyalty to her. An intense duel erupted as Opress and Ventress tried to kill Dooku, but it escalated into a three-way confrontation when Opress broke free of Ventress's control and turned on both of his former masters. Evading Opress, Ventress pursued Dooku to the lower decks. But even in single combat, she was unable to defeat the Sith Lord. Ventress barely made it into an escape pod, and she departed from Dooku's dreadnought, now facing an uncertain future.[204]

Meanwhile, Opress again encountered Kenobi and Skywalker after they reached Dooku's dreadnought aboard the Thief's Eye, the personal yacht of the late Katuunko. When Dooku's battle droids opened fire on them in the main hangar, Opress and his Jedi adversaries escaped separately from the cruiser, bringing the showdown to an end. Opress limped home to Dathomir, where Talzin sent him on a quest to save his long-lost brother Maul,[204] who had once been Sidious's apprentice[63] and was in fact Talzin's son.[211]

Citadel prison break

"There have not been battles like these since the days of the Old Republic."
―Saesee Tiin[64]
Main article: Battle of Lola Sayu

A year and nine months into the Clone Wars,[217] the Nexus Route—a little-known hyperspace lane that connected Coruscant with the heart of Separatist space—gained critical importance for both the Republic and the Confederacy. When Jedi General Even Piell and his crew unearthed the coordinates of the Nexus Route, the Confederacy targeted him for capture. As a Confederate flotilla overwhelmed his Star Destroyer, Piell divided the Nexus Route's coordinates with his naval captain, Wilhuff Tarkin. Both of them memorized half of the information as a safeguard against torture. The Separatists thereafter abducted Piell, Tarkin, and their clone navigation officers and incarcerated them in Lola Sayu's infamous Citadel prison, which was being overseen by Warden Osi Sobeck.[32]

After receiving word of Piell's capture, the Jedi High Council assembled an infiltration team to rescue him and his crew from the Citadel. Kenobi and Skywalker received command of a squad of clone troopers, with additional support from Commander Cody, Captain Rex, and ARC troopers Echo and Fives. Much to Skywalker's later consternation, Ahsoka Tano joined the mission even though he ordered her not to do so. At the Jedi Temple, the Jedi and clones encased themselves in carbonite to mask their life form signatures from the Confederacy's blockade of Lola Sayu. The dangerous operation began when R2-D2 and a squad of reprogrammed B1 battle droids transported the Jedi and clones to[32] the Lola Sayu system[14] aboard a pilfered Sheathipede-class shuttle. Once they had bypassed the blockade and reached Lola Sayu's surface, R2-D2 unfroze his comrades from their carbonite blocks.[32]

Despite Tano's unexpected appearance, Kenobi and Skywalker let her join their operation. After free-climbing a cliff to reach the Citadel, the infiltration team rescued Piell, as well as Tarkin and their clone officers. Along the way, they evaded Sobeck's countermeasures, which ranged from wall-mounted blaster cannons and electrical emitters, to elite BX-series droid commandos. Nevertheless, the squad incurred casualties from Sobeck's traps. As part of their plan's next stage, Kenobi and Skywalker divided their forces. While Skywalker and Tano brought Tarkin, Rex, Fives, Echo, and several troopers into the caverns beneath the Citadel, Kenobi, Piell, Cody, and the other soldiers created a diversion by exploding one of the Citadel's upper decks.[32] Yet, complications arose as both squads headed to their separate extraction points. R2-D2 and his reprogrammed droids landed the shuttle at the Citadel's rear landing pad, but Sobeck's tactical droid, K2-B4, intercepted them there. Moreover, Sobeck recaptured Cody, Kenobi, Piell, and their men, but R2-D2 and his battle droids freed them from Sobeck's droid security teams.[218]

To reach their extraction point at the Citadel's external fuel pipeline, Skywalker, Tano, Tarkin, and their soldiers used thermal detonators to rupture a blocked cavern as well as a pursuing squad of battle droids. However, when R2-D2 and the shuttle missed their scheduled rendezvous, Skywalker and Tano resorted to their backup plan. After using more of their explosives to detonate the fuel in the exterior pipeline, Skywalker, Tano, Tarkin, and their men proceeded to the prison's main landing pad. They arrived at the airfield just as Kenobi, Piell, and their squad mounted a desperate offensive to eliminate the battle droids that had separated them from their shuttle. While Kenobi, Piell, Skywalker, and Tano concentrated on destroying an incoming squad of battle droids aboard Single Trooper Aerial Platforms, Echo and Fives focused their attention on the ground-level enemy infantry. Yet, just as Echo tried to board the shuttle, a droid commando fired a turret blast at the craft, causing a fiery explosion that consumed the shuttle and, presumably, Echo.[218]

Without their shuttle, the four Jedi escaped from the Citadel's airfield with Tarkin, as well as Cody, Rex, Fives, and their remaining troopers. As they made their way across Lola Sayu's inhospitable terrain, Kenobi and Skywalker notified the Jedi High Council that they would require an extraction from Lola Sayu.[218] Consequently, the Council sent four of its members—Kit Fisto, Adi Gallia, Plo Koon, and Saesee Tiin—to the Lola Sayu system with a battle group of four Star Destroyers. In the meantime, Piell and his allies headed for an island that the Council had selected as their extraction point. En route, an endless number of battle droid squads pursued the Jedi and clones, leading R2-D2 to sacrifice his reprogrammed battle droids to delay the enemy forces as long as possible.[64]

It was not long before Sobeck personally took charge of the effort to recapture his prisoners. Under pressure from Dooku to recover the Nexus Route intelligence, Sobeck dispatched a hunting party of ravenous anoobas to locate the Jedi and clones, then followed with a squad of droid commandos. Although the Jedi and clones defeated Sobeck's anoobas and LM-432 crab droids, their momentary victory came at a severe cost. Piell died from fatal wounds from one of the anoobas, using his final breaths to pass his half of the Nexus Route coordinates to Tano. She and her comrades took a brief respite from the battle to lay Piell to rest, cremating his body in one of Lola Sayu's rivers of sulfurous lava.[64]

Shortly thereafter, Fisto, Gallia, Koon, and Tiin arrived in the Lola Sayu system with their fleet of Star Destroyers. While Admiral Barton Coburn commanded the Republic fleet's assault on K2-B4's blockade of warships, Fisto, Gallia, and Tiin served as wing commanders and, in their Delta-7B interceptors, escorted Koon and Commander Wolffe's space gunship so that they could extract their comrades from the surface. Koon and Wolffe reached the appointed rendezvous point just after Sobeck arrived there with his battle droids to recapture Kenobi, Skywalker, Tano, Tarkin, and their soldiers. Frustrated by his prisoners' periodic evasion of recapture, Sobeck simply decided to kill Tarkin to ensure that his half of the Nexus Route intelligence died with him. Yet, Tano saved Tarkin by igniting her shoto lightsaber through Sobeck, killing him. Tano and her allies then escaped with Koon and Wolffe aboard their gunship, and all of them safely returned to Coburn's fleet with Fisto, Gallia, and Tiin. The Republic armada jumped to hyperspace, thereby resulting in a major defeat for the Confederacy.[64]

On Coruscant, the Jedi Council was saddened to learn of Piell's sacrifice. Moreover, the Jedi encountered difficulties before they could debrief the Nexus Route coordinates. Whereas Tarkin had orders to provide his half of the information directly to Sheev Palpatine, Tano remained committed to Piell's dying wish that she deliver her share of the coordinates only to the High Council. Master Yoda subsequently met with Palpatine to figure out a solution to the matter. The entire incident also led Skywalker and Tarkin to find common ground based on their similar criticisms of the Jedi Code and the Jedi Order's role as generals.[64] In addition, though Echo was presumed dead during the escape from the Citadel,[219] he had in fact survived.[220] The Techno Union purchased Echo from the Separatists and subjected him to extensive reconstructive surgery, fusing him with a large amount of cybernetics as part of a research project.[221]

Civil war on Mon Cala

Main article: Battle of Mon Cala

Following the murder of Mon Calamari King, Yos Kolina, the Separatists and the Republic sent representatives to assist in the ascension of a new king. The Jedi Council then sent Master Kit Fisto and Commander Ahsoka Tano to reinforce Anakin Skywalker and the Mon Calamari Guard against the Quarren's and Tamson's forces.[33]

Tamson countered this when he rallied his Trident ships to create whirlpools around the battle sites. Lee-Char stabbed Tamson with one of the knives and shot it, killing the Separatist warlord and leaving his remains to sink.[43]

Failed peace conference on Mandalore

"The Republic recognizes the tragedy of war, but there is nothing we can change that has already occurred."
"Say it aloud before this gathering—as representative for Chancellor Palpatine that you declare, without reservation, the Separatist state legitimate."
―Senators Padmé Amidala and Voe Atell[174]
Main article: Confederate–Republic peace conference

In an effort to end the Clone Wars, the Republic and Separatists held their first ever sanctioned peace conference on Mandalore, as the planet was neutral ground. Many held hope for the meeting, and Senator Amidala, who was joined by Padawan Tano, was one of the Republic's representatives. During the conference, after Confederate Senator Voe Atell demanded her to, Amidala was reluctant to declare the CIS a legitimate government. At that moment, however, their meeting was interrupted by the uninvited Lux Bonteri, who told those assembled that his mother Mina had been killed by Count Dooku. Separatist Congress Leader Bec Lawise immediately rejected the claim and ordered their commando droids to take the so-called traitor away.[174]

Afterward, while Lawise was willing to continue the meeting, Amidala secretly allowed Tano,[174] who had met Bonteri during Amidala and Mina's earlier peace initiative,[56] to follow the droids, as the Jedi Padawan knew her friend's life was in danger. Unknown to her, Bonteri had planned on being captured, as he had wanted to get Dooku's attention. Believing they were a noble group, Bonteri had allied with Death Watch, who also wanted revenge on the Count, and planned on using a holotrace device to locate Dooku, which would allow Death Watch to attack him.[174]

Brought into a C-9979 landing craft by the pair of commandos, Bonteri was dropped before a hologram of the Count. While Bonteri was able to activate his holotrace device, Dooku ordered the droids to kill the young man, but, after the Count's hologram deactivated, Tano entered the room and took out the commandos. During their escape, Tano contacted R2-D2, ordering him to activate the engines on their GX1 short hauler, the Phoenix, and she and Bonteri were chased by a force of commando droids. Staying ahead of the droids, they reached the starship and were given covering fire by Captain Taggart's forces.[174]

Aboard the GX1 with R2, they spoke with General Skywalker over hologram, who revealed the peace conference had all but collapsed. Although Tano intended to bring Bonteri to safety on Coruscant, where she and Skywalker could discuss giving the former Separatist amnesty, he zapped her unconscious and took the Phoenix to Death Watch on Carlac. During their time there, Bonteri gave the holotrace to Pre Vizsla, but he also saw the group's true colors when they burned a Ming Po Town. With the help of a group of droids Death Watch had been keeping as target practice, he, Tano, and R2 escaped the terrorists. Thinking he could not go with her, Bonteri still refused to go to the Republic and, after promising Tano that he would see her again, left the Phoenix aboard an escape pod.[174]

Cortosis plot

Involvement of the Chiss and Grysks

One month before the mission to Batuu, R2-D2 was shot by a B2-RP super battle droid when he had wanted to see what was unfolding; it had then taken technicians three days to rebuild R2.[48] Meanwhile, the Chiss Ascendancy, an empire that controlled part of the Unknown Regions,[224] kept watch on the rest of the galaxy[48] and came to learn that a massive war was being fought there. Though their reports were unconfirmed, the Chiss also learned that one side largely used droids in combat. During the Nikardun conquests they faced at the same time as the Clone Wars, Chiss Senior Captain Mitth'raw'nuruodo, also known by his core name of "Thrawn," and Force-sensitive sky-walker navigator Che'ri journeyed into the galaxy to search for allies against the Nikardun. Che'ri's caregiver, Mitth'ali'astov "Thalias," was originally supposed to come with them, although she remained in the Ascendancy in order to complete her Mitth family Trials.[2]

After finding nothing of value on the first four worlds they checked, Thrawn and Che'ri spotted a force of Separatist droid starfighters stationed at[2] the planet Mokivj. The Confederacy had taken over Mokivj after a then-unknown species—the Grysks—provided intelligence to Dooku by telling him the metal cortosis could block lightsaber strikes. Dooku dispatched Duke Solha, as well as the Duke's brother and sister, to oversee a cortosis mine and droid factory, the latter producing[48] the C-B3 cortosis battle droid,[225] a B2-series super battle droid with cortosis armor able to block blasters and lightsabers. To the confusion of the Grysks, the factory also produced clone trooper armor made from cortosis, as Darth Sidious planned to use the metal to help in the execution of Order 66. The factory was protected by a deflector shield,[48] which Thrawn spotted and realized could be of great use to the Ascendancy.[2]

Directly afterward, Thrawn and Che'ri spotted another ship watching the droid starfighters, so the Senior Captain ordered Che'ri to navigate their ship to the first planet they had investigated in order to get there first, reasoning that, by being the most populous, it was the most likely destination for the other craft to rendezvous or send a message from. Indeed being the first to arrive at the planet, which was the Outer Rim world of Batuu, Thrawn sent a communication in several trade languages to the other ship after it emerged from hyperspace, introducing himself as a Senior Captain of the Ascendancy and getting an answer in Meese Caulf, the second-to-last trade language he had used. The pilot of the other ship was Duja,[2] who had been a handmaiden to Padmé Amidala and had uncovered the Separatist conspiracy unfolding on Mokivj. As such, she sent that information to Amidala.[48]

Nevertheless, in addition to rotating her ship slightly so she could fire upon the Chiss if need be, she only told the two her name before asking whether the Chiss supported the Republic or Confederacy. When Thrawn clarified that their government served neither, she decided she had no reason to speak with the Senior Captain, only asking if he had seen a Nubian ship arrive. When Thrawn confirmed they had not, Duja ended their conversation, leaving Thrawn with the feeling she was a scout or spy. As he explained to Che'ri, who had expected him to call Duja back, her armed ship and slight rotation confirmed she had training, but he understood she was not a warrior. Thus, he reasoned the two of them would wait until a warrior arrived.[2]

Mission to Batuu
«This is no longer merely a search for a missing ambassador. It's become an important part of your Clone War. Remember that victory is the goal.»
―Senior Captain Thrawn, to Anakin Skywalker[48]
Main article: Mission to Batuu

Having received Duja's vague message that there was some kind of Separatist operation around Batuu, Republic High Command found the report too vague to act on, so Amidala decided to investigate it herself. Although she told Skywalker of her plan, noting that she would not be alone because of Duja's presence on Batuu, her husband was unable to go with her, needing to serve as the leader for an upcoming battle. Skywalker also claimed to her that the Clone Wars would indeed end one day, but he understood that everyone was questioning if the conflict would end, with only the Chancellor holding the Republic together. Promising to spend time with him once she returned, Amidala departed, and Skywalker went onto lead the battle; like many others, the engagement saw minor advancements and losses amid destruction and death. Skywalker's forces were weary after the end of the battle, returning to Coruscant after it, and Skywalker found that Amidala had yet to return nor had she sent any messages.[48]

With Dooku making another advance, the Jedi Council denied Skywalker's request to search for her, as he instead had to fight in another, albeit quick, battle. When he returned to Corsucant again, still without any messages, Skywalker uncovered that her Nubian ship was abandoned on Batuu.[48] From space, Thrawn and Che'ri had seen Amidala's ship approach, with it arriving three days after they had spoken with Duja.[2] Amidala had tried to send messages to her husband, but Skywalker had not received them. After learning that Duja had died, Amidala retrieved a beacon call from her fallen friend's brooch, teaching her that the Separatist operation was a factory. She departed Batuu, which was only being used by Separatist smugglers to get supplies to the factory, aboard Duja's ship, the Possibility,[48] a few hours after she had arrived. Thrawn and Che'ri saw the ship depart, with the navigator waiting for Nubian to follow it, only to see it remained hidden on the planet below. Days passed before[2] Skywalker arrived out of hyperspace, flying his Eta-2 Actis-class light interceptor with R2-D2.[48]

Seeing the hyperspace transport ring the Eta-2 had used to exit hyperspace, Thrawn had his ship move closer to it in order to study it, which caught the attention of R2-D2 and Skywalker. Not wanting to lose his way out of the system, Skywalker sent out a transmission in Galactic Basic Standard before repeating it in Meese Caulf, asking for the identity of the crew and identifying himself. While he responded, Thrawn doubted Skywalker's claim that he was on a mission, understanding that a government at war would not send a lone starfighter. Lying by insisting he was not on a personal quest, Skywalker claimed that Palpatine, who actually did not know Skywalker was at Batuu, had sent him on the mission, understanding that the man he was speaking with likely knew of the Chancellor if he knew of the war. When Thrawn revealed he knew where the Nubian was, having deduced Skywalker was looking for the ship, he offered an alliance, claiming to be alone before Skywalker felt Che'ri's presence through the Force. Nevertheless, Thrawn went onto mention his "pilot" before learning R2 would be joining them for their mission. Upon the Chiss explaining he wanted to know more about the Clone Wars before it could sweep in the Ascendancy's own worlds, he also finally introduced himself.[48]

However, Thrawn claimed to be a commander, instead of stating his actual rank of Senior Captain, and never mentioned his desire to take the shield generator[2] from Mokivj. Skywalker agreed to the alliance, hoping the Ascendancy he now knew of may become an ally to the Republic. While Skywalker elected to fly down to Batuu in his Eta-2, Thrawn elected to take a shuttle to lead the way to the Nubian's location,[48] as he ordered Che'ri to take their ship back to the Mokivj system so that, when he arrived, she could fly down to retrieve the shield generator. He ordered her to use as many decoys as needed to keep the droid starfighters away once he signaled her.[2] Upon landing, after he fought a group of smugglers who had found the ship, Skywalker investigated the Nubian while Thrawn and R2 remained outside to search for clues. All three then departed for Black Spire Outpost aboard Thrawn's shuttle.[48]

Devastation of Mokivj

In time, Skywalker and Thrawn learned of the smuggling operation for Mokivj, which they learned was under the command of Solha, and that a ring of thieves was stealing from the operation. Before leaving Batuu, Skywalker informed Thrawn about Dooku, Grievous, and Palpatine, and Thrawn advised him to remember that, in war, his goal should remain victory instead of revenge. On Mokivj, Amidala, having crashed landed the Possibility after being attacked by a vulture droid, bribed three locals named Cimy, Huga, and LebJau to keep her presence a secret, and Thrawn, Skywalker, and R2 landed at the Separatist factory with the captured CIS freighter Larkrer, initially pretending to be its crew before they were captured. The Chiss and Jedi ultimately escaped their improvised cells. Joined by Huga and Cimy, Amidala, who had witnessed the arrest of her husband and his allies, and her allies disguised themselves as maintenance workers to head to the detention block, with the Senator taking out two B1 battle droids guarding it. Upon entering, she united with Skywalker and Thrawn. As Skywalker served as a distraction, Amidala and Thrawn journeyed to retrieve the Jedi's lightsaber.[48]

Amidala also convinced Lebjau to evacuate the workers for their plan to destroy the factory. Skywalker found himself in the B2 assembly line, where he saw Solha, his brother, and his sister in suits of clone trooper armor. As Skywalker distracted the duke and his forces in the assembly room, Thrawn and Amidala found Skywalker's lightsaber, but the Chiss used the blade to cut out the shield generator core, claiming he had been given a mission to retrieve the generator. While Amidala protested the idea of him leaving, Thrawn remained steadfast in his commitment to the Chiss and additionally asked why the Republic had not allowed the Confederacy to secede peacefully. After she stated the Confederacy had attacked first, Thrawn advised her to use the south end's door before she was out of his sight.[48]

However, Thrawn made sure to return to helping shortly afterward, wielding a lightning gun to help take down the cortosis B2s. He also explained what the metal, which Skywalker had realized—in his battle against the droids—could resist lightsaber strikes, was and how it was rare. Additionally, the team elected to discover what the northern wing of the factory was producing. After R2 worked to reprogram the B2 factory, Amidala was confronted by Solha, while Skywalker and Thrawn uncovered the north wing was producing cortosis-weaved clone armor; Skywalker quickly assumed Dooku was planning a mass-Serennian infiltration of the clone army as a surprise attack. After Amidala knocked out Sophla, Skywalker ensured the factory was destroyed, yet he also sought to destroy the Cortosis mine. Thrawn confided to Amidala that he believed the Jedi General's plan was reckless, arguing that it would be better for the CIS to waste resources on Mokivj than to make them to look elsewhere.[48]

Although she agreed, the Senator understood that her husband could not be talked out of his plan, even though Thrawn warned her it could be a threat to Mokivj. He also declined her offer to return to Coruscant with them to create a more formal Chiss—Republic alliance, stating he had other duties to attend to and that he was not tasked with such a role. Before departing, Thrawn also advised them that the clone armor may have not been intended for an infiltration, as such operations had a high risk of failing. Although Thrawn disagreed, Skywalker was certain that they did not need to worry about the plan. Skywalker's plan to collapse the mining tunnels would indeed have unintended consequences; as he, Amidala, and LebJau, who had asked to leave with them to start a new life on Batuu, watched from their ship, the cortosis redirected the explosives' heat, causing a catastrophe that, despite not moving towards the people of Mokivj, would devastate the environment of the world. While Amidala promised they would talk to the Senate about providing aid, all three understood it would do nothing, and they departed from the planet.[48]

Upon his return to the Republic, Skywalker told Palpatine about Thrawn and praised the tactician. Thrawn, meanwhile, respected Skywalker greatly,[98] although he had come to the conclusion that the Republic was not a suitable ally for his people.[224] Additionally, he used the shielding technology from Mokivj to great effect in the battle over Primea, blocking blasts from the Nikardun Battle Dreadnought Deathless in order to board its bridge. After the Chiss victory in that battle, the Nikardun Destiny and its conquests came to an end.[2] Rumors of a blue alien forming an alliance with Skywalker also spread in the galaxy, with the story coming to reach at least as far as the Thrugii asteroid belt.[98] Rather than correctly report[225] on Skywalker triggering the catastrophe that devastated Mokivj,[48] Clone Intelligence reported that the Chiss Expansionary Defense Fleet was responsible for the catastrophe.[225]

Last days of the Republic

Final days of democracy

"Thank you all for attending. I know we can count on the signatures, but I've invited this group to discuss the exact wording of the petition."
"In broad strokes, our demands are that Chancellor Palpatine relinquish the emergency war powers granted to him, abolish the Sector Governance Decree, and begin cease-fire talks with Count Dooku's Separatists."
"Are we going too far? The war is popular in my sector. We would be seen by many as obstructing an inevitable victory."

―Bail Organa, Mon Mothma, Terr Taneel, and Padmé Amidala discuss the Petition of 2,000[226]

Thanks to the Emergency Powers Act from the beginning of the Separatist Crisis, Palpatine remained in power for the entirety of the Clone Wars,[41] although his prolonged time in office did begin to draw suspicion from the Jedi as the war reached its end[8] and relations between the Jedi and the Chancellor continued to break down.[62] As per his plans to transform the Republic into an autocracy with himself at its top,[8] Palpatine used the Clone Wars to further cement his political power and undermine the democracy[227] he claimed to represent.[15] By the end of the war, Maul had come to believe the Republic was long since dead and there was nothing the Jedi could do to save it.[228] Indeed, while senators like Mon Mothma, who would oppose Palpatine's power grabs, were distracted by the conflict with the Separatists, Palpatine, Amedda, and his other supporters waged a war of their own in the field of public relations, securing the love and mandate of the people.[17]

Palpatine managed to amend the Galactic Constitution again and again, always using the war as his excuse[226] to secure more power for himself.[229] Although the Enhanced Privacy Invasion Bill was defeated in the Senate,[13] a number of other emergency war powers were passed,[226] with Palpatine becoming the most powerful chancellor since the Ruusan Reformations. In particular, four amendments to the constitution were cemented in law: one of the four was the Reflex Amendment, which granted Palpatine expansive powers by ceding near-total power over the Republic Military to Palpatine, who could thus bypass the Senate on military decisions.[41] The Sector Governance Decree was an amendment passed near the end of the war on the claim that it would bring unity and sure up the supply line; under the decree, Palpatine was granted the ability to name individuals[118] regional governors,[226] who would then unify neighboring star systems and focus their resources on the production of war materiel.[118]

In practice, however, the existence of regional governors served to circumvent the power of the Senate by creating a new group of officials,[230] named by Palpatine himself,[118] with power over star systems.[230] Despite Palpatine's efforts to consolidate power attracting criticism from some senators, most defended it as a necessary evil in the name of defeating the Confederacy, which Dooku exercised near-total control over.[41] Dooku's own war powers saw opposition from his senate's Peace Faction,[13] but he continued to enjoy wide support amongst the Confederacy overall.[21] However, the Sector Governance Decree proved to be the final erosion of senatorial authority for a group of like-minded senators who became known as the Delegation of 2,000. Under the leadership of Senators Organa, Amidala, and Mothma,[41] who specifically recognized Palpatine as a threat to democracy but failed to understand the scope of his ambitions,[226] the group created a formal petition[41] known as the Petition of 2,000 in protest of the Chancellor's conduct[231] and acquired powers.[41]

Broadly, the petition had three demands: Palpatine was to give up his emergency powers[226] by returning those powers to the Senate at the end of the war,[231] abolish the Sector Governance Decree in particular, and open a cease-fire with the Confederacy. In what would end up being the final month of the war,[226] the three leaders of the delegation[41] began the Cantham House meetings by gathering a select number of like-minded senators to discuss and finalize their petition,[226] which they intended to present once it acquired two thousand signatures. By its end, the Clone War was losing the support of the public. The conflict brought great suffering, war taxes, and rationing, with even the Core Worlds being affected.[41] Although the war remained popular in the Senex sector, whose people saw a Republic victory as an inevitability,[226] a number of other senators faced great pressure from those they represented to push for peace. However, powerful lobbyists in the Senate managed to vote down those efforts in order to protect their war profits.[41]

While she was indeed worried about Palpatine's growing power,[232] Senator Terr Taneel of the Senex sector was nervous about pressing for the end of the war and noted as such during a Cantham House meeting, citing her sector's support for the conflict. Amidala, however, defended it as necessity to both stop the bloodshed and Palpatine's excuse for creating amendments.[226] The delegation backed public calls for Palpatine to abandon his increased power as their public tactic. The group secretly prepared itself to go beyond the Senate and form a resistance effort should that be needed.[233]

Battle over Coruscant

"Ahsoka, surely you understand this is a pivotal moment in the Clone Wars? The heart of the Republic is under attack!"
―Obi-Wan Kenobi, to Ahsoka Tano[95]

The super tactical droid General Kalani would state his calculations showed the Separatists were on the verge of victory at the war's end.[234] Alternatively, the war's third year made others assume that the Republic now held all of the momentum.[53] Ultimately, however, both sides were in crisis by the end of the war.[8][53] The Republic was crumbling due to Separatist attacks ordered by Dooku,[8] while the Separatists had been pushed back to the spiral arms of the galaxy. A campaign called the Outer Rim Sieges would result in most of the Republic's Jedi and military forces fighting on these outer worlds.[53] However, another part of the sieges occurred when Grievous launched a massive assault that pushed the Republic Military to the brink, so Jedi Generals were also sent far from the Core Worlds to help the clone army because of that offensive.[95]

Ultimately, while the Republic had begun to overwhelm the Separatist armies and the Confederacy had lost much of its territory, with what remained being targeted in the sieges,[235] Grievous's overwhelming offensive was still a threat,[95] and the Republic Army was also engaging in desperate campaigns across the galaxy, while the Separatists were encircling the Republic, moving ever-nearer to the systems of the Core.[100] Nevertheless, despite being a bitter stalemate for a time,[236] the sieges would ultimately turn the tide of the conflict to be in the Republic's favor.[237]

During the Outer Rim sieges, Kenobi, Skywalker, and their troops captured Yerbana from the Confederacy. Following the victory, one of their "Fulcrum" contacts reached out to them. At first, Skywalker believed it was Gerrara requesting aid from the Republic due the Siege at Onderon. In was revealed that Fulcrum was Skywalker's former apprentice, Ahsoka Tano. She was working with Lady Bo-Katan Kryze and the Mandalorian resistance in tracking down Maul[95], following his brief capture[6] and escape from Lord Sidious on Dathomir.[238] Kryze informed Kenobi and Skywalker that Maul was in Sundari according to transmissions between the Pykes and Maul. Kenobi and Skywalker were willing to speak the Jedi Council on this matter and help her.[95]

During the final days of the conflict, the Republic space station Sentinel Flare was attacked by the Confederacy, which left the station severely damaged.[239] Prior to the war's end, Jedi General Weren Dal was shot down over Dathomir by an elite Separatist group.[240] Due to most Jedi and clones fighting in the Outer Rim, the Republic's capital of Coruscant was left relatively undefended. However, Republic strategists did not worry. They believed the Separatists would not dare attack the capital, but under the orders of Sidious, Grievous and Dooku launched a massive assault on Coruscant. The inexperienced Coruscant Home Defense Fleet was taken by surprise, and Grievous was able to sneak onto the surface of the planet.[53]

Grievous eventually managed to capture Palpatine and hold him hostage (which was what Sidious ordered him to do as well). Sidious orchestrated Palpatine's capture in order for Skywalker to kill Dooku, which would tempt him to the dark side and lead to him becoming his apprentice, as Sidious felt the time had come and Dooku's purpose had been served, although both Dooku and Grievous were unaware of the Sith Lords' true intention. Grievous brought the Chancellor back to his flagship, the Invisible Hand.[8] After sending the 332nd Division under Commanders Rex and Tano to assist Lady Kryze in hunting Maul Down on Mandalore, Kenobi and Skywalker took their forces to Coruscant.[95] The large-scale naval battle between the Separatist and Republic forces continued, and during this attack Kenobi and Skywalker raced to save the Chancellor. Dooku was defeated by Anakin and subsequently betrayed by Sidious, who as Palpatine, had him killed by Anakin.[8] Dooku's death was a massive blow to the Separatists and left Grievous as its new Head of State.[53] The Separatists, however, were unaware that Sidious orchestrated Dooku's death. The Jedi managed to escape the ship along with the Chancellor. Grievous also escaped and fled to the planet Utapau.[8]

Aftermath

The new era

"I take it we met during the Clone Wars—and that you were on the side of the "Republic." I wonder… How do you like your Republic now? Understand, as a Separatist, I fought for freedom but put my trust in a corrupt leadership."
"You were the leadership—a General."
"The Jedi were Generals. Do you truly believe they comprehended the cause they served? Holster your weapon, boy. We are no longer enemies. Perhaps we never were."
―Separatist General Kleeve to surviving Jedi Commander Caleb Dume[243]

The cataclysmic[100] Clone Wars had raged for three,[244] almost four, years by the end[245] and accomplished exactly what Palpatine had set out to achieve; the Jedi Order was slandered and destroyed, the Republic was transformed into the first Galactic Empire, and the Galactic Senate into the Imperial Senate, with Palpatine as its Emperor.[8] Nevertheless, during the following early months of the Imperial Era, the Clone Wars were not entirely over, as minor pockets of resistance, including a force of rebels on Umbara, continued to fight the Republic's successor state. Accordingly, the newly formed Imperial Military was dispatched to crush these remaining obstacles to bring about the Empire's view of peace.[11] The galaxy at large, however, welcomed the Empire as a way to move forward from the destruction and devastation of war. Miyuki Trade League member Jet Kordo was not surprised by the rise of the Empire, but reflected solemnly in a journal that they did not expect the people of the galaxy to wake up to the price they were paying in return for the conflict's end.[246]

In the aftermath of the conflict and with the dawn of the Empire, Senator Organa reflected that he was unsure if there was a "right side" to the Clone Wars. In regards to the CIS, he still opposed what he deemed the cruel, destructive tactics of the CIS military and the greed of its corporate sponsors, but he did recognize there were well-meaning people amongst the Separatist state. Nonetheless, he still believed that non-violent routes had still been open for the Separatists instead of deciding to go to war. As for the Republic, meanwhile, he had come to ponder if the war had been a misdirection of sorts by those in the government who already wanted to transform the government into the Empire. He recognized that Palpatine and his followers had pushed for the fighting[17]—something Palpatine had tried to cover up with public apprehension about going to war[11]—and had his own thoughts on Dooku, although he believed the particulars of Dooku's situation were not as important. Overall, he was forced to admit that, by taking part in the war, himself and everyone else involved had played into Palpatine's plan to establish the Empire.[17]

The last remnants of the Confederacy, known as the Separatist holdouts, continued to fight the Empire.[11] The Imperial Navy justified its existence by claiming there was an unending war against the holdouts and a dissident rebellion against the Empire.[100] Imperial stormtroopers were deployed to bring former Confederate planets under the Empire's control;[14] even the former CIS capital world of Raxus Secundus fell under occupation during the early reign of the Empire.[20] A day into the Imperial Era, sixty-three members of the Delegation of 2,000 were arrested by clone troopers on the claim that they had helped the Jedi rebellion. Organa and Mothma were among those arrested but were released by publicly declaring their loyalty lied with the Empire,[226] which both continued to serve as senators. In secret, both used their positions as senators as a cover for rebellion.[247][248] Amidala's death, meanwhile, was blamed on the Jedi rebellion.[249]

Also during the early reign of the Empire, the future Grand Moff Wilhuff Tarkin led a brutal purge on the moon Antar 4 that became known as the Antar Atrocity. Imperial forces rounded up and killed many Koorivar and Gotals including Republic loyalists. Media coverage of the Antar Atrocity attracted considerable outrage in the Core Worlds and forced the Emperor to reassign Tarkin to overseeing the pacification operations in the Western Reaches. The brutality of the Antar Atrocity prompted other former Separatist worlds such as Kooriva, Murkhana, and Raxus to surrender former Separatists to the Empire to avoid the same fate as Antar 4. Tarkin's actions earned him the animosity of former Republic Intelligence operatives Berch Teller and Knotts, who founded a insurgent group consisting of survivors and witnesses of the Antar Atrocity. In 14 BBY,[250] Berch Teller's cell embarked on a campaign against Tarkin and the Empire, but it was defeated.[1]

In 2 BBY, a last unofficial skirmish occurred when the Spectres rebel cell encountered a Separatist holdout of still functioning battle droids, led by the super tactical droid Kalani, while attempting to scavenge the wreckage of a Separatist supply ship. Kalani took the Spectres prisoner and, upon confirming that the group contained Clone Captain Rex, who had joined with the rebellion instead of supporting the Empire, Jedi Knight Kanan Jarrus, and his padawan Ezra Bridger, forced them to run through a tactical scenario, intending to prove that the Separatists had a higher chance of victory and end the Clone Wars with a victory for the Confederacy.[234]

Following its creation, the Galactic Empire tried to sweep away the memories of the troubled times of the Clone Wars[22] but also used the memory of the conflict to justify its expansion; the Empire expanded its reach across the galaxy, using the memory of the Clone Wars by promising order to a galaxy tired of war.[252] After it became clear that the Empire was oppressive, however, the Rebel Alliance was created to oppose the Empire's rule.[253] The seeds of the Alliance dated back to the Clone Wars: its roots came from the local resistance cells established by the Jedi on Confederate worlds and from the Delegation of 2,000, fulfilling that group's fear that armed resistance would be needed to restore democracy.[233] Palpatine's victory in the Clone Wars lasted just over two decades, as the Galactic Civil War led to the fall of Palpatine and his Empire, as well as the redemption of Anakin Skywalker who renounced the persona of Vader, before dying peacefully.[254]

Many Imperials—such as the ambitious Imperial Navy officer Thrawn, the very same Chiss who had met Anakin Skywalker during the conflict—remembered the Clone Wars as the cause of billions of deaths, hundreds of destroyed worlds, and thousands of ruined worlds clawing back from the brink. He regarded secessionist movements such as the one on Botajef as a repeat of that horror. His colleague Eli Vanto believed that the Clone Wars had bred animosity between humans and aliens since several alien species had fought on the side of the Separatists. While several aliens had fought on the side of the Republic, this sentiment gave rise to a level of xenophobia within the human-dominated Empire. Thrawn was even reprimanded by his superior, Filia Rossi, the captain of the Blood Crow ship, for having equipment used by the Separatists in his possession.[98] Droids were also suspect in some beings' eyes; Din Djarin, for example, hated all droids because Separatist battle droids had destroyed his family.[255]

The Empire also housed veterans of the struggle in poorly maintained places like Crispus Commons, where they were forced to deal with shabby maintenance and low-paying jobs. The conspiracy behind the conflict had not yet been brought to public light, and nearly the entirety of the galaxy's population believed the war to have been exactly what it had seemed; a rebellion initiated by numerous worlds of the Mid and Outer Rims desiring independence from a corrupt and decadent central government. Despite this, some, such as Skelly, pieced together there was a greater truth about the Clone Wars.[22] Some individuals took part in historical re-enactments of the Clone Wars and there was also a section on the Clone Wars in the Emperor's Museum on Coruscant and although they used real footage they told a false history, which was seen by the Apprentice Legislature on a tour in 3 BBY.[256]

Wilhuff Tarkin also remained suspicious of the cause of the war even after its conclusion, and believed that some group of elite outsiders had manufactured the war for their own purposes.[1] There were those, such as Bail Organa, who remembered the bravery of those like the Jedi Knights during the Clone Wars who passed this knowledge to his daughter, Princess Leia Organa[230] as well as the stories such as that of the Senate hostage crisis as well as several about Obi-Wan Kenobi.[256] Leia would later sent a holographic message to Kenobi appealing to him in the name of his service alongside her father during the Clone Wars.[230] A couple of months after the Battle of Endor, a Separatist droid factory under the city of Myrra on Akiva still had marks of Jedi lightsabers.[96] It remained one of the most destructive conflicts in galactic history, with billions of casualties on both sides.[257] After Sidious's ultimate defeat in the Battle of Exegol of 35 ABY,[213] historian Beaumont Kin carried out the Exegol Excavation Project and discovered the extent of Palpatine's treachery in the Sith records, publishing his deception and manipulation of the Clone Wars in his historical book The Rise and Fall of the Galactic Empire.[258]

Behind the scenes

The Clone Wars were first mentioned in canon in the 1977 original Star Wars film, Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope.[230] The canon details of the conflict were first revealed in the prequel trilogy films Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones[15] and Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith.[8]

The first reference to the Clone Wars dates back to George Lucas' third draft for Episode IV, which mentioned the grizzled cyborg General Kenobi's "diary of the Clone Wars."[259] The passing mentions of the Clone Wars in A New Hope were the only mentions of the conflict in the original trilogy.[230] In Leigh Brackett's first draft of the script for the 1980 sequel Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back, Lando Calrissian was a clone from a clone planet that was nearly ravaged in the Clone Wars.[260]

The Clone Wars was first adapted in Star Wars: Clone Wars in 2003, which has since been retconned by the inception of the 2008 film Star Wars: The Clone Wars, as well as the animated television series by the same title.[91] By 2014, both The Clone Wars film and the television series are part of the Star Wars canon, as they reflected the vision of Lucas.[261][262]

In the attempt to keep the Star Wars toy line active after the final film in the original trilogy, Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi, Kenner Products devised a toy extension entitled The Epic Continues that would have involved the return of an exiled "genetic terrorist" known as Atha Prime, one of the architects of the Clone Wars, and his Clone Warriors.[263] In Attack of the Clones, it was seen that Darth Sidious and Count Dooku fill that role.[15]
